features.name: articles and stories
features.what: your words, with covers and rows of photos.

features.name: project pages
features.what: a page for each thing you make.

features.name: site search
features.what: search across your articles, stories and steps.

features.name: your work, live
features.what: your repositories and commits on /founders, through a GitHub App you own.

features.name: steps people follow
features.what: a curriculum people sign in to, with their progress saved.

features.name: a members area
features.what: /party, for the people you let in from your waitlist.

features.name: an admin panel
features.what: your steps, users and submissions in /admin.

features.name: build by describing
features.what: say what you want; Claude Code reads your copy, writes the change, and you review it.
features.ai: a large language model predicts the next words from everything it has read. pointed at your files, that means it can explain them and draft changes. it can be wrong, so you read before you keep.

features.name: sell a project
features.what: a buy button on a project page. Polar takes the payment, and the buyer's account remembers it.

features.name: photo prompts
features.what: steps people answer with a photo, collected in /admin.

features.name: waitlist emails
features.what: one when someone joins, another when you let them in.

features.name: approve from Slack
features.what: a message for every sign-up, with approve and reject buttons.

features.name: theme songs
features.what: a song on every article, played without leaving the page.

features.name: your own analytics
features.what: which pages people read and which requests break, in /admin.

features.name: answers from your notes
features.what: search that answers from your docs and notes, not only your pages.
features.ai: retrieval: the search finds the passages that match the question, then the answer is written from them, so it stays close to your own words.
